scope: Read-only causal-control design and source/object audit. No compile, consumer execution, product change or timing in this design step.

existing_control_comparison.callbacks_and_storage: Stage8 plain_bench.cc differs from canonical only by twoHyleHarness accessors and raw_write single-attempt parameter/branch. RawEndpoint/RawStream/RawHeader, nghttp2callbacks/options, body buffers/checks, window consumes and wire payload copy functions are otherwise the same source.
existing_control_comparison.wire_initialization: Both canonical manual run_raw and stage8 Episode contain TWO RawWire objects; EACH has64KiB pending plus64KiB input with value initialization. Total explicit wire-array zero initialization is256KiB per rawcold episode in BOTH. It is not an extra256KiB unique to the fiber control. Actual compiler memset/DSE was not separately measured.
existing_control_comparison.wire_placement: Manual wires live on RawHarness worker stack. Stage8 Episode/wires live on externalcaller stack outside its two64KiB fiber stacks; this changes placement/first-touch/allocator context despite same source capacities.
existing_control_comparison.extra_fiber_owner_work: Stage8 adds sharedEpisode/Event/failure state, TcpStream::adopt/bind wrappers, twoendpointTask/JoinHandle/ownedfiber lifecycles, perendpoint EndpointCleanup, server wait forclientconsumed, and perendpoint session destruction/socket wrapper teardown. Manual uses RawHarness CV dispatch and central cleanup after its dual-endpoint loop.
existing_control_comparison.initialization_and_teardown_order: Canonical initializes client thensever together on rawworker and centrally deletes bothsessions/closesfds. Stage8 initializes each inside its endpointTask and deletes/closes there; interleaving, thread and order differ.
existing_control_comparison.driver_difference: Stage8 splits advance_client/advance_server, flush-reentry and singletry afteryield to matchHyle cadence; bounded adaptiveyield plus perendpoint asyncfallback. Canonical retains dual-endpoint fill/write/read/consume cycle and poll2fds only when neither progresses. Equal payload and successfulIO counts do not make syscall ordering or hostwork identical.
existing_control_comparison.conclusion: Stage8 Hyle-vsraw2fiber close results are a useful restricted control, not a pure contextswitch cost or an explanation by subtraction of current16-17percent manual-loop residual.

smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.recommendation: A separate restricted oneScheduler-worker control, same commonRawEpisode owner and same canonical rawprotocol functions in both arms: one spawnedTask executes canonical manual dual-endpoint loop versus two spawnedTask endpoint drivers. Keep original public-vsmanual ranking unchanged.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.common_cold_owner: Inside BOTH timedcallbacks create the same socketpair and TcpStream adoptions, same stack-resident Episode on externalcaller, same twoRawWire value initialization, endpointstream reserve, and client/server raw_initialize in identical order. Keep caller-owned state alive through alljoins.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.common_protocol: Reuse one copy of canonical callback/header/body/wire functions; do not clone/forkcallbacks. Existing splitadvance helpers must remain exact corresponding halves of canonical raw_advance. Same nativeallocator/options, bodyverification, reverse pair, fullACK/EOF/endstream responsibilities.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.common_cleanup: After alljobs join, perform identical server/clientcompletion checks, delete both native sessions and close both adopted sockets in the same sharedcleanup order/context; do not retain oldperendpoint EndpointCleanup as a second teardown policy.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.manual_arm: Spawn ONE job on the sameScheduler/owner, running the original raw_advance plus client/server fill-write-read-consume ordering and dual-fd poll fallback. Coordinatorjoins thatjob.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.two_endpoint_arm: Spawn twojobs on thatsameworker; each owns onlyits endpoint and uses existing bounded-yield/readiness fallback, with common terminal coordination so server is not closed before client consumes. Coordinatorjoins both.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.resources: Same persistentScheduler+IoContext and inactiveRawHarness thread exist forbotharms; all inherit sameaffinity. Protocol IO occurs on sameScheduler worker, unlike comparing rawworker protocol with schedulerworker protocol.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.what_is_variable: One versus twoTask/fiber/JoinHandle lifecycles, cooperative endpoint scheduling, retry/syscall cadence and readiness policy. Extra driverallocation/wakes are part of the independent variable, not storage changes to be hidden.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.what_cannot_be_claimed: It intentionally gives the controlmanual arm oneTask and commonadoption/owner placement absent from originalpeer. It is not a zeroTask baseline, originalpeer ranking or pure fcontext cyclemeasurement. Completely identical syscalltrace/readiness/handoffs cannot be guaranteed while changing this driver strategy.
smallest_reasonable_new_control_design.bounded_validation_if_later_authorized: Onlysame4x256KiB completeepisode perarm first, verify fullpayload/reverseACK/session/socket teardown. No generalizeddriverframework or matrix; any counts are eventfacts, not timeattribution. No implementation currentlymade.

concrete_private_helper_cost.source: src/io_http2/http2.cc:2392-2445 send_submitted_fixed has no co_await but returns Task<Status> and is awaited by both public fixedsendTask entrypoints.
concrete_private_helper_cost.task_semantics: include/hyle/sched/coro.h:66-85 allocates frame via AllocatorRef;153-167 nestedTaskawaiter drives todone on same stackfulfiber. This does not imply an extra Scheduler contextswitch for everyTask.
concrete_private_helper_cost.compiled_fact: Existing measured GCC14/O3 http2.o has two direct caller actor calls tofactory0xdaa0. Factorymov0x100 toesi then allocator indirectcall at0xdb09 requests256B/alignment16. Staticdisassembly only, not a new runtimeallocation probe.
concrete_private_helper_cost.normal_episode_bound: 4request sends plus4response sends invoke8 privateframes, nominal2048B requested and8 allocation/free lifecycles, apart from publictasks and transportfallbacktasks. This is not perbodychunk and not elapsed-time explanation.
concrete_private_helper_cost.minimum_fix: Return ordinaryStatus from privatehelper, retaining allocator parameter because drive_until forwards it to fallbacktransport tasks. Keep publicTask signatures/allocator/pins/error/owner/spanlifetime unchanged; directcall thehelper from the twopublicTasks.
concrete_private_helper_cost.do_not_delete_allocator: The parameter is not solely a frameallocator: it is forwarded todrive_until and transportread/write Task allocation. Changing it tostate.allocator could change lowlevelentry allocationdomain.
concrete_private_helper_cost.other_limits: body.consume already has a singlecoroutine and calls synchronousread_body perchunk; do not claim oneframe perDATA fragment. Runtime allocationcounts outside this confirmedfactory were not measured.
